text:
anya: quick check — we're onboarding PartnerX for embeddings. They want us to talk to their private endpoint in their VPC via a peering connection. Do we prefer VPC peering + SG rules or a NAT + allowlist? Also, how do we ensure logs don't contain plaintext input tokens (PII) when egressing?

leo: my vote is peering if possible — avoids public egress and IP rotation issues. but peering means we need strict SGs and route table controls. NAT can be simpler for short term.

shawn: +1 on peering for production. for short-term testing we can do NAT with an allowlist of their egress IPs (but that's brittle).

anya: agreed. if peering, who needs to approve? network team? compliance?

leo: network & sec. we'll need an architecture doc + security review. I'll sketch a small diagram and SG rules.

security-bot: reminder: before any peering, run the restricted-ports checklist and fill out the PrivateNetworkApproval form: https://internal.redwood/corp/risk/forms

anya: good call. on logging: current app logs request metadata including client_ip, url_path, and full prompt in DEBUG logs. we should redact prompt content before persisting. any recommended approach?

shawn: yes — strip prompt bodies in app-level logging and send a hashed prompt_id instead. keep telemetry for latency and tokens but never raw prompt. example middleware we use:

```python
def redact_for_logs(req):
    req_meta = {
        'route': req.path,
        'prompt_id': sha256(req.body[:64]).hexdigest(),
        'token_count': token_counter(req.body)
    }
    return req_meta
```

leo: also ensure any structured logs sent to logging infra have a redact field set so log-retention jobs can scrub accidentally stored fields. update SSO/KMS policy if logs go to partner-managed sinks.

sre-oncall: FYI, if we route via peering, flow logs might capture src/dst IPs. that's fine, but annotate the flow-log retention and set exclusion for payload fields (they don't have payloads but note for auditors).

anya: action items I got: 1) leo will draft architecture + SG rules and submit PrivateNetworkApproval. 2) shawn will add middleware to redact prompts and swap DEBUG to a safe mode. 3) I'll coordinate with PartnerX on peering timeline.

leo: i'll ping network for a timeslot. tagging @shawn for review of the SGs when ready :eyes:

shawn: will review. also can we add a canary rule to fallback to NAT/allowlist if peering fails? small egress policy with lower throughput.

anya: yes, plan to add fallback. thanks all :thumbsup:

security-bot: checklist reminder: include threat model snippet, flow-log retention, and data-handling notes in the approval ticket.
